title:
The whole bloody history.
 
 Nightmare from which you will never awake.
html_source:
This, being Stephen’s stream of consciouness that springs everynow and then in this chapter intercalated with Bloom’s own thoughts, is a direct reference to a line, spoken by the own Dedalus, in chapter 2, http://genius.com/James-joyce-ulysses-chap-2-nestor-annotated.

The line is: History is a nightmare from which I am trying to awake.

History is a recurring motif in that chapter, since Stephen is giving a class about Pyrrhus, a Greek general and statesman. Also, it alludes a conversation he and Haines had on the preciding chapter, where the englishman says that he feels that England has “treated you rather unfairly”, talking about the colonization of the irish people by the english.

So, this thought of Stephen not only shows his pessimistic view from the current state of Ireland as it also is an insight of his own life: the improductive time he spent on Paris and his mother’s death.

History (of Ireland) is not the unique nightmare, but also his own life, which he can’t awake from.

Stephen goes deeper on his feelings about the death of his mother, Paris and his own solitude on the chapter Proteus.
